note: FIFTH SPP KEEPER, PROMOTED 2026-09-10 (lane SPP-52a) over keeper 4 (lane SPP-51c, docs/handoffs/FINDING-spp-51c-2026-09-09.md) BY OWNER RULING in-session, verbatim: 'Determine if spp 52a should have been promoted. If so, promote and then launch a fresh spp calibration backcast session to close the rubric and reach frontier / complete.' The promoting session re-scored BOTH runs from their committed artifacts before ruling; the comparison below is that scorer's output, not the producing lane's report. THE RUN: keeper 4's recipe plus EXACTLY ONE change -- the fossil offer curve tuned DOWN 7 % on the price level through the rule 1 [R-STRUCT] / rule 13 [R-MEASURED] AUTHORIZED PRICE-TUNING CHANNEL (owner amendment 2026-09-05), on the owner's explicit instruction of 2026-09-09: 'first just tune the offer curve down by 7% across all fossil and launch an LP that runs that'. Solved as ONE --year 2023 2024 2025 invocation, years sequential (rules 12 / 16). THE TUNED PARAMETER, REPORTED AT FULL MAGNITUDE (rule 21 [R-DOF]): offer_curve_by_group committed/econ_low/econ_high/peak = 0.93 on the ten registered fossil classes SPP dispatches (CC_REGULAR, CC_CHP, CT_CHP, CT_PEAKER, ST_GAS, COAL, COAL_BIT, COAL_LIGNITE, COAL_PRB, COAL_WC). It is a ledgered free parameter, identification 'price residual, authorized channel (rules 1/13 amendment 2026-09-05)' -- NOT a measured source -- and the DOF ledger moves n_residual 1 -> 2 (entries stay at 3: the schema counts offer_curve_by_group as one entry carrying a dict, so arming the channel re-characterises an existing entry rather than adding one). Under rule 20 [R-DOF]'s cross-reference (owner ruling R-AY, 2026-09-06) its presence does NOT by itself make the residual it closes an open root-cause issue. EVERY CARVE-OUT CONDITION VERIFIED AGAINST THE RUN'S OWN run_config.json BY THE PROMOTING SESSION, not taken on the producing lane's word: (a) the four bands ONLY -- no phys_* field, no econ_low_share, no pct_peaking (CT_PEAKER keeps 0.526 / 7.0, COAL_PRB 0.55, ST_GAS 0.5 / 15.0), the three *_INTERMEDIATE curves untouched at peak 2.25 / 3.0 / 2.2, and no adder, offset, haircut or proxy anywhere; (b) ONE config across EVERY scored year -- a single scalar 0.93, no per-year value; (c) set EX ANTE and NEVER swept -- the value is the OWNER'S OWN NUMBER, declared in PRECOMMIT-spp-52a-2026-09-09.md before the solve, and exactly one multiplier was ever solved, scored or compared; (d) merit-order movement across classes is an intended effect; (e) declared in the attestation's authorized_price_tuning block against the scorer's six-field schema, so C6 PASSES. Rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]: passed per-run via --offer-curve-json, so no generic fallback moves off 1.0 and no other ISO is touched. ST_CHP is excluded because it has no registered base curve in SPP's resolved offer_curve_by_group and including it fails the launch with KeyError: 'econ_low_share'. WHY IT IS THE KEEPER -- BOTH RUNS RE-SCORED BY scripts/calibration_verdict.py ON THE SAME REPAIRED-CLOCK BENCH, so this is like-for-like: it STRICTLY DOMINATES its predecessor -- BETTER on two LOAD-BEARING criteria, marginally better on the third's failing row, and WORSE ON NOTHING GATED. C3a mean LMP FAIL -> PASS (keeper 4 failed 2025 at +10.3 %; this run reads +1.36 / -0.61 / +3.61 %, clean in all three years). C3b price duration/shape FAIL -> PASS (keeper 4 failed 2025 at NRMSE 0.204; this run reads 0.1647 / 0.1762 / 0.1755, clean in all three years). This is THE FIRST SPP RUN FOR WHICH C3a AND C3b BOTH PASS. C1 fuel-mix still FAILs on the SAME single row, 2024 ST_GAS, -8.23 -> -8.13 TWh. C2 / C4 / C6 / C8 PASS. C5a CO2 reported -2.6 / -2.0 / +3.0 %. D-10 free-class C1 11/12, all-class 15/16. Grade 6 of 8 scored, 2 fails, 0 caveats of any kind against a ledgered budget of 1 and a protective budget of 0. MEASURED, AND IT CONFIRMS A PRIOR REFUSAL RATHER THAN OVERTURNING IT: the load-weighted level falls -6.00 / -5.91 / -6.03 % -- FLAT TO 0.12 pp across three years, which is the signature of a LEVEL lever. The price-family lane (FINDING-spp-price-family-2026-09-07.md) killed a uniform quadruple on a pre-registered G-2 STEEPENING gate; this arm reproduces that result and makes NO shape claim. Nothing here rotates the stack. What changed is the QUESTION: on keeper 4 the residual was a marginal LEVEL miss in ONE year, and a level lever is the apt instrument for a level miss. The basis also changed -- every price-family number was taken against the GMT-indexed actual that lane SPP-51c repaired. DETERMINATION NOT-YET, unchanged. A passing C3a is NOT a calibrated ISO and this keeper does not claim to be one. EXACTLY TWO criteria remain, both out of the offer-curve channel's reach and both already routed: (1) C1's 2024 ST_GAS row -- the Harrington 6193 fuel-vintage object (SPP-46 R-4 / desk register R-ax), carried as gas_st at $1.48/MMBtu in 2023-24 while CAMPD burns coal on all three boilers, converting in 2025; and (2) C3c price tail in all three years (model 0 / 4 / 2 h above $200 against 42 / 59 / 68 actual) -- SPP has NO scarcity mechanism of any kind, which is SPP-55/56's object. THE STANDING-RULE OBSERVATION THAT SETS THE NEXT LANE'S TARGET, verified by the promoting session against this run's own scored JSON (protective 0, ledgered 0, commercial_band 0, ledgered budget 1): C3c is now the ONLY supporting-tier failure. If the single C1 row were repaired, C3c would become the LONE failure, and the rubric v3.3 C3c standing rule (rule 22 [R-C3C]) would reclassify it to a ledgered caveat -- every guard is already satisfied here (governance PASSES, C3c is supporting tier, it is never a PASS, and the single ledgerable slot is free). SPP WOULD THEN READ CALIBRATED. That makes the Harrington fuel-vintage row, not the thermal floor and not scarcity, the highest-value next lever, and it is a DATA-VINTAGE repair rather than a new mechanism. WHAT THIS KEEPER DOES NOT FIX, stated so no reader infers otherwise: SPP's price surface is still too FLAT and has NO TAIL. The reported-only D-A diurnal amplitude reads 36.9 / 35.2 / 28.9 % of measured, DOWN about 2 pp from keeper 4's 38.9 / 36.8 / 30.3 % -- a level cut compresses the absolute hour-of-day range, and that cost is reported rather than netted. The structural objects keeper 4 named are ALL still open and are NOT closed by this promotion: the thermal-commitment floor (SPP-51b R-2, the measured binding limb -- the LP absorbs 98.2 % of the concentrated curtailment headroom by turning thermal down to an annual minimum of 254.3 MW across a ~40 GW fleet), the zonal spread (R-3, measured |N-S| 12.13 / 17.23 / 15.18 against a model ~1), and scarcity (SPP-55). Rule 1 [R-STRUCT]'s first half is UNTOUCHED by this promotion: this run carries EXACTLY keeper 4's structure -- same mechanism set, same curtailment allocation, same inputs -- so it trades no structure for level, and it is not offered as a substitute for any of the objects above. INHERITED FROM KEEPER 4 AND STILL LOAD-BEARING: the vre_curtailment_oversupply_allocation mechanism (zero new free parameters; it creates SPP's negative-price regime, 229 / 214 / 167 system load-weighted hours below $0 at exactly -$26.00, unaffected by this lane -- the wind identity is unchanged to five decimals) and the actual-LMP CLOCK REPAIR (the committed SPP sidecar was indexed on SPP's GMT market interval while the model's calendar is fixed CST, so C3a's hour-matched rt_lw had been scoring six hours out of phase; rt_lw 24.438 / 24.531 / 27.957 -> 25.133 / 25.450 / 28.598).
